speaker_role: independent counselor / essay coach (College Essay Guy)
commercial_incentive: Sells one-on-one coaching through College Essay Guy; mentioned at the end.
key_insights: He outlines a seven-part structure: core values, why you chose your current school, why it did not work, how you made the best of it, future goals, school-specific fit, and a short sign-off.
Explain the original reason for choosing the current college plainly; not every paragraph has to be poetic.
When explaining why it fell short, give claim plus concrete evidence and avoid trash-talking; complaining looks bad and vague criticism undermines your logic.
Show resourcefulness by describing what you did about the gaps, such as starting a club or study group.
If the plan was always to transfer, frame it as having completed the purpose of the first school.
Name specific courses, professors, and opportunities and say what you want from each; niche courses show deeper research.
If a school has a separate why-us essay, keep the transfer essay general and put specifics there; otherwise customize one paragraph per school.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Reuse plan: write five general paragraphs and swap only the school-specific sixth for each school.
notable_or_distinctive: A paragraph-by-paragraph transfer essay blueprint, uncommon compared with first-year essay advice.
reliability_notes: Advice is one coach's framework without admissions-office confirmation; examples are anonymized student samples.
